{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Karen Linda Collins''' is an American mathematician at [[Wesleyan University]], where she is the Edward Burr Van Vleck Professor of Mathematics, Chair of Mathematics and Computer Science, and Professor of Integrative Sciences.{{r|wesleyan}} The main topics in her research are [[combinatorics]] and [[graph theory]].

Collins graduated from [[Smith College]] in 1981,{{r|wesleyan}} and completed her Ph.D. in 1986 at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. Her dissertation, ''Distance Matrices of Graphs'', was supervised by [[Richard P. Stanley]].{{r|mg}} In the same year, she joined the Wesleyan faculty.{{r|vv}}

She was given the Edward Burr Van Vleck Professorship in 2017.{{r|vv}}
